newsitem.title: THAILAND: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Sept 13.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Thai newspapers - Sept 13.

text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the Thai press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Pressure intensifies from partners in the coalition government for the prime minister to resign. But sources in Prime Minister Banharn Silpa-archa's Chart Thai party said there are growing indications he will dissolve the parliament instead of stepping down, although it is not clear if it will be done before or after next week's censure debate. (BANGKOK POST)

- The daily minimum wage in Bangkok and neighbouring provinces will rise 12 baht to 157 baht on October 1 following an agreement by representatives of government officials, employers and employees. (BANGKOK POST)

- Permanent Secretary for Defence General Paiboon Emphan says Defence Minister General Chavalit Yongchaiyudh ordered the review of a proposal to purchase 225 armoured personnel carriers from France. (THE NATION)
- Officials inspecting roadside food quality have found animal saliva and urine in cooked and fresh food sold at food stalls and markets throughout Bangkok. (THE NATION)
- Finance Minister Bodi Chunnananda is to consider a proposal on abolishing the maintenance margin system in the stock market in order to shore up the bourse. (MANAGER)
- The property market in Bangkok continues to be sluggish, with 21 percent of the total space of office buildings remaining vacant during the first half of this year. (THAI THURAKIJ FINANCE)
- SET leaps three percent as investors hunt for bargain stocks. Market sentiment imprived slightly as investors plunged back into the market to take advantage of the more upbeat mood. (BUSINESS DAY)

- BMW AG and its Thai partner Yontrakit Group form a joint venture which will take over the wholesaling of BMW cars and motorcycles from January. The new link is aimed at boosting the German car maker's presence in Thailand through an improved dealer and after-sales network, BMW chairman says. (BANGKOK POST)
